[[def-cm13-canonical-map]] defines the dimension-aware canonical maps of the
presentation by $C^{*}\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}$; a lower-dimensional map is a
symplectic immersion, while equal-dimensional maps have the matrix test
$DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$ and determinant consequence $|\det DC|=1$.
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]] proves that
the Hamiltonian evolution itself is canonical on its actual time-slice
domains — the two-form, the bracket and the determinant are preserved locally
in time, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time. Its time slices have the
$C^1$ regularity stated there; the separate fixed-map field-transport
theorem applies to an individual time slice only when it has additional
$C^2$ regularity.
[[pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canonical-maps]] proves that an
equal-dimensional local canonical transformation conjugates Hamiltonian
fields and transports the model's Hamiltonian systems and brackets.
[[pthm-cm13-liouville]] uses the phase-volume form
$\Omega=\omega^{\wedge n}/n!$ to prove conservation of phase volume: on its
actual domains the Hamiltonian evolution preserves the Lebesgue measure in
every full-dimensional canonical chart, under the stated Axiom of Countable
Choice used by the change-of-variables step. The phase-volume unit is action
to the power $3N$. [[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] closes the
constructive part: first- and second-kind generating functions with
nondegenerate mixed derivative generate canonical local diffeomorphisms of
the presentation, the local converse holds under an invertible
$(q,Q)$-projection, and a time-dependent generating function carries the
identity $p\cdot dq-H\,dt=P\cdot dQ-K\,dt+dS$ with $K=H+S_{t}$ and transports
Hamilton's equations between the two descriptions; the underlying calculus
of generating functions is that of [[cm-math-canonical]].

   momentum. The second-kind relations are
   $\pi=S_q=DX(q)^{\mathsf T}P$ and $Q=S_P=X(q)$, so solving for $P$ gives

   consequently $\Phi_X$ is a canonical map of the presentation with

[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]] constructs on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ a smooth nondegenerate
Lorentzian metric $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ whose restriction to $r>s$ is the exterior
datum; the level set $r=s$ is a smooth null hypersurface with generator
direction $\partial_v$, and the Ricci tensor and Kretschmann scalar of
$g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ extend smoothly across it. In the Kruskal model
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]], [[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]]) the full level set $\{r=s\}$ is $\{UV=0\}=\{U=0\}\cup\{V=0\}$.
Each axis times $S^2$ is a smooth hypersurface: $dU$ and $dV$ never vanish,
and the inverse base matrix has $g^{UU}=g^{VV}=0$, so each has null normal
covector. They intersect transversely at the **bifurcation sphere**
$\{U=V=0\}\times S^2$. Their tangent spaces there together span the full
four-dimensional tangent space, so their union cannot be a smooth
three-dimensional hypersurface at that sphere. The function $r$ and metric
remain smooth there; the curvature invariant is $12/s^4$ on both axes.
For future escape to the right exterior, the boundary is specifically
$\{U=0\}$, while $\{V=0\}$ is the past escape boundary. The one-way
character in the model is the exact statement of
[[lem-gr-kruskal-causal-escape-and-trapping]] clause (d): no future-directed
causal curve issued at a point with $U\ge0$ reaches the quadrant
$\{U<0,V>0\}$ with $r\to+\infty$, while every point with $U<0$ admits such a
curve along the future radial null geodesic at constant $U$. This is a causal
property of the smooth model; it is not a divergence of the metric at the
surface, and the model's time orientation is part of the datum.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, fix a compact interval $I_0$ inside the coefficient time domain, and let $J\subseteq I_0$ be an interval on which the Galerkin solution is defined. Let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$, and let $u_N:J\to X_N$ be a Galerkin
solution ([[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]]) with $u_N(t)$ taking values
in $K$ and $\|u_N(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$ for all $t\in J$. Define the **weighted
energy**
$$e(t):=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\int_{\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}}\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}A^0\bigl(t,x,u_N(t)\bigr)\bigl(D^\alpha u_N(t)\bigr)\,d\mu(x).$$
Then:

[L2] The Galerkin equation $P_N[A^0(t,\cdot,u_N)\partial_tu_N+A^i(t,\cdot,u_N)\partial_iu_N+B(t,\cdot,u_N)]=0$ holds in $L^2$; $P_N$ is self-adjoint, commutes with $D^\alpha$ and acts as the identity on $X_N$ ([[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]], [[lem-gr-galerkin-projection-properties]]).

[L4] Write $\dot A^0=\partial_t A^0(t,x,u_N)+\partial_u A^0(t,x,u_N)[\partial_tu_N]$, the total coefficient derivative. It is uniformly bounded in $L^\infty$ by the time derivative bound and embedding. The spatial coefficient derivatives have the same boundedness. Moreover $e$ is continuously differentiable: $u_N\in C^1(J;X_N)$, the coefficients are smooth and $t\mapsto A^0(t,x,u_N(t))$ is $C^1$ uniformly on the compact torus, so differentiation under the finite sum and the integral is legitimate, giving $e'(t)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le s}\int\bigl[2(D^\alpha\partial_tu_N)^{\mathsf T}A^0D^\alpha u_N+(D^\alpha u_N)^{\mathsf T}(\dot A^0)D^\alpha u_N\bigr]d\mu$ ([[lem-gr-galerkin-ode-local-solution]], [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]).

and determinant tests of canonicity on each two-dimensional block and the

[[ex-cm13-free-particle-flow-generating-function]] exhibits the free-particle
flow $Q=q+(t/m)p$ as generated by the first-kind action function
$S_{t}(q,Q)=-m\lvert Q-q\rvert^{2}/(2t)$, with the projection check and the
exact change of the canonical one-form.
[[ex-cm13-point-transformation-generating-function-and-projection]]
generates the point-transformation chart transition
$(q,\pi)\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\pi)$, from generalized momentum $\pi$
to Cartesian momentum, using the second-kind action function $S(q,P)=P\cdot
X(q)$. It shows that the $(q,Q)$-projection is nowhere invertible, so the
local converse's invertible-projection hypothesis cannot be dropped; the
momentum shift supplies the contrast. [[ex-cm13-determinant-tests-for-linear-canonical-maps]]
proves on explicit linear maps that $\det A=1$ is equivalent to canonicity
in dimension two but strictly weaker in dimension four, by the
volume-preserving shear with $\{Q^{2},P_{1}\}=1$.

the velocity-Verlet step of the model's mechanical splitting is a canonical
map of the presentation: the drift and kick are exact flows with unit
determinant, their composite preserves the two-form, and the oscillator
instance is computed explicitly.

consumer_reviews.affected_use:
The two counterexamples exhibit the hypotheses that cannot be dropped.
[[cex-cm14-harmonic-model-critical-fibre]] shows that the zero-energy
level of the one-degree-of-freedom harmonic datum in its declared
generalized-coordinate presentation is a compact connected common level
set that is a single point, not a torus: compactness and connectedness
alone do not give the toral conclusion, regularity is indispensable.
[[cex-cm14-free-particle-noncompact-fibre]] uses the three-integral free-particle datum
$(H,p_1,p_2)$ on $p_3>0$: each common fibre at
$(E,c_1,c_2)$ with $2mE>c_1^2+c_2^2$ is a connected copy of
$\mathbb R^3$ that is
noncompact and carries no period at all, so the compactness hypothesis of
[[pthm-cm14-regular-tori]] is indispensable too. The published
mathematical obstruction
[[prop-period-lattice-monodromy-obstructs-global-action-angle-coordinates]]
and the refuted global statement
[[fs-liouville-arnold-gives-global-action-angle-coordinates-on-the-entire-manifold]]
record the complementary global failure: local action-angle coordinates
need not patch to a single-valued global chart even when all fibres are
regular and compact, so no universal torus chart is claimed. Finally,
[[ex-cm14-oscillator-caustic-check]] exhibits the local caustic of the
oscillator family: the mixed derivative $S_{x\alpha}$ of the complete
integral is unbounded at the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$,
and the family of model solutions through a fixed event refocuses there,
which is why the Hamilton–Jacobi statements of this page are local in
time and carry no claim across a caustic.

consumer_reviews.affected_use:
[[ex-cm16-pendulum-equilibrium-checks]] works the ideal pendulum in the angle
chart with $m=1\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\ell=1\ \mathrm m$ and
$g=9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$: the downward equilibrium is a strict minimum,
hence Lyapunov stable and not attracting, with the purely imaginary
linearisation frequencies $\pm i\,3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$; the upward
equilibrium has the negative Hessian $-mg\ell$ and is unstable, with the real
rates $\pm3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
[[ex-cm16-linearization-and-growth-checks]] computes the flows and growth
rates of two dimensionless one-label Cartesian models in $\mathbb R^3$: the
harmonic force $F(\mathbf q)=-\mathbf q$ has an orthogonal rotation flow, so
every finite-time growth rate vanishes and every existing Lyapunov exponent is
$0$; the repulsive force $F(\mathbf q)=\mathbf q$ has exact rates $\pm1$ along
its eigendirections and positive Lyapunov exponent $1$ at equilibrium.
[[ex-cm16-isotropic-oscillator-return-map-check]] shows the
three-dimensional isotropic force model's stroboscopic map at half period to
be minus the identity on its six-dimensional phase space: every state is
periodic, the periodic points are dense, but the map is neither topologically
mixing nor sensitive, so continuous maps with dense periodic points need not
be chaotic in the page's stated sense.
[[ex-cm16-pulse-horseshoe-data-check]] evaluates the constants of the pulsed
horseshoe on its invariant axis at $a=100$: the coding box $R=13$, the
radicands in $[74,126]$, the contraction factor $1/\sqrt{74}$, the fixed
points $1\pm\sqrt{101}$, the limiting kick composition, and the axial physical
bounds $13\ \mathrm m$ and
$26\pi\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ at $\ell_0=1\ \mathrm m$, $m=1\ \mathrm{kg}$,
$\omega_0=2\pi\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

consumer_reviews.affected_use:
The chaos material is built on the two local mathematical supplier pages
[[cm-math-chaos]] and [[cm-math-kam]].
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] fixes one precise chaos list for the
stroboscopic, Poincare-return and autonomous time-one maps on invariant
domains: continuity, topological mixing, dense periodic points and
sensitive dependence. This item makes no pairwise-independence claim and
records that fixed linear coordinate rescalings preserve the list; numerical
portraits do not establish its clauses. [[pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horseshoe]]
then adopts a smooth $P$-periodic one-label force model on full Cartesian
configuration space $\mathbb R^3$: the pulse acts on an invariant axis, and
the two transverse directions have explicitly adopted inverted-oscillator
forces. For every pulse width below a threshold depending only on the
dimensionless amplitude $a\ge100$ and the bump, the full physical stroboscopic
map has a compact invariant set on the axis conjugate to the two-sign shift
and chaotic in the stated sense; its fixed points are hyperbolic in the full
six-dimensional phase space and its homoclinic points are transverse there.
The coded states satisfy the bounds $\lvert Q\rvert\le R\ell_0$ and
$\lvert\Pi\rvert\le m\ell_0\omega_0R$ with $R=\sqrt a+3$. The countable and
dependent choice assumptions are inherited from the supplier and declared.
[[pthm-cm16-two-rotor-kam]] treats the complementary nearly integrable
two-rotor model with the adopted potential $E_0\varepsilon\cos\theta_1
\cos\theta_2$: for every Diophantine exponent $\tau>1$ and a constant $c>0$
determined by the declared dimensionless data, every $0<\alpha<c$ and
$0<\varepsilon\le c\alpha^2$ give a positive-measure set of Diophantine
frequencies whose tori persist as $C^1$ Lagrangian embeddings carrying
quasi-periodic motion with physical angular frequencies $\omega_0\nu_i$
($\omega_0=\sqrt{E_0/\mathcal I}$); the complement of that set, resonant gaps,
chaotic diffusion and all empirical realizations are explicitly out of scope.
Finally [[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]], under the
countable choice assumption inherited from the phase-volume theorem, proves
Poincare recurrence at unit time steps for a bounded invariant Borel set with
compact closure in an autonomous potential phase domain and a flow complete on
that set. Its proof extends local phase-volume preservation by a finite cover
and time subdivision; the conclusion is almost-everywhere, with no return-time
or individual-state claim.

downstream_uses.rem-gr-schwarzschild-horizon-and-singula:
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]] constructs on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ a smooth nondegenerate
Lorentzian metric $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ whose restriction to $r>s$ is the exterior
datum; the level set $r=s$ is a smooth null hypersurface with generator
direction $\partial_v$, and the Ricci tensor and Kretschmann scalar of
$g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ extend smoothly across it. In the Kruskal model
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]], [[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]]) the full level set $\{r=s\}$ is $\{UV=0\}=\{U=0\}\cup\{V=0\}$.
Each axis times $S^2$ is a smooth hypersurface: $dU$ and $dV$ never vanish,
and the inverse base matrix has $g^{UU}=g^{VV}=0$, so each has null normal
covector. They intersect transversely at the **bifurcation sphere**
$\{U=V=0\}\times S^2$. Their tangent spaces there together span the full
four-dimensional tangent space, so their union cannot be a smooth
three-dimensional hypersurface at that sphere. The function $r$ and metric
remain smooth there; the curvature invariant is $12/s^4$ on both axes.
For future escape to the right exterior, the boundary is specifically
$\{U=0\}$, while $\{V=0\}$ is the past escape boundary. The one-way
character in the model is the exact statement of
[[lem-gr-kruskal-causal-escape-and-trapping]] clause (d): no future-directed
causal curve issued at a point with $U\ge0$ reaches the quadrant
$\{U<0,V>0\}$ with $r\to+\infty$, while every point with $U<0$ admits such a
curve along the future radial null geodesic at constant $U$. This is a causal
property of the smooth model; it is not a divergence of the metric at the
surface, and the model's time orientation is part of the datum.
downstream_uses.rem-nrqm-bell-boundaries-and-comparison-:
- **What the comparison establishes.** For the declared spin correlation
  arrangement of [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], the four sign
  tables are the laws $\nu^{\rho}_{ij}(\varepsilon,\delta)$ of clause (d) of
  that definition. If the arrangement's CHSH functional satisfies
  $|S(\nu^{\rho})|>2$, then the four tables admit no local-response model:
  every local-response representation would give $|S|\le2$ by
  [[thm-nrqm-bell-local-representations-satisfy-chsh]]. The singlet at the
  directions of [[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] is the
  displayed instance, with $|S|=2\sqrt2$. The statement is a conditional
  no-go for one precisely defined class of models of one precisely defined set
  of four tables.

- **Assumptions used.** The deduction rests on the framework readings P1, P2,
  P3, P5, P6 and P7 fixed by
  [[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]], on the declared composite,
  preparation and spin-half assignments, on the ideal sharp character of the
  declared measurements ([[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
  on the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom
  of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) stated in the arrangement and
  singlet-attainment hypotheses, and on the cited mathematics (the
  finite-dimensional tensor calculus, the CHSH bound for representable models
  and the operator bound of
  [[pthm-nrqm-bell-tsirelson-bound-for-arrangements]]). Changing one of these
  readings voids the conditional conclusion for the changed model; it does not
  weaken it, and a replacement conclusion needs its own proof.

- **No-signalling is not the separator.** Every local-response model is
  no-signalling ([[prop-nrqm-bell-local-representations-are-no-signalling]]),
  and every declared arrangement's marginals are also setting-independent:
  summing its joint law over $\delta$ gives
  $\nu^{\rho,A}_{ij}(\varepsilon)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(P_{a_i,\varepsilon}\otimes I))$
  because $\sum_\delta P_{b_j,\delta}=I$, and the symmetric sum is
  $\nu^{\rho,B}_{ij}(\delta)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I\otimes P_{b_j,\delta}))$
  ([[def-nrqm-bell-declared-spin-arrangement]] clauses (a), (d)). For the
  singlet both marginals are $1/2$
  ([[texp-nrqm-bell-singlet-arrangement-contrast]] clause (d)); a discarded
  declared local instrument on one factor leaves the other factor unchanged
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b)).
  The contrast between the two classes therefore lies in the joint tables,
  not in any dependence of one station's marginal law on the distant setting.

downstream_uses.rem-nrqm-uncertainty-energy-time-caveat:
**What the framework does support.** The graph-domain Ehrenfest theorem
[[thm-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-graph-domain-ehrenfest-and-timescale]] is a
conditional mathematical statement about a curve
$\psi:I\to H$ that is $C^{1}$ into the graph norm of a self-adjoint $A$, stays
in $D(AK)$ (and in $D(KA)$ where stated), has unit norm and satisfies
$\psi'=-\tfrac{i}{\hbar}K\psi$. Under those hypotheses, with
$f(t):=\langle A\psi(t),\psi(t)\rangle$ and $f'(t_{0})\ne0$, the timescale
$\tau_{A}(t_{0}):=\Delta A(t_{0})/|f'(t_{0})|$ satisfies
$$\Delta K(t_{0})\,\tau_{A}(t_{0})\ge\frac{\hbar}{2}.$$
With $K=H$ the energy, the Heisenberg-picture theorem identifies $f'(t_{0})$
with the derivative of the mean of the representative observable when $A$ is
bounded and preserves the energy domain,
$A D(H_{\mathrm{op}})\subseteq D(H_{\mathrm{op}})$
([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-heisenberg-picture]] clause (c)). Boundedness
alone does not imply this domain-invariance condition. For a domain-qualified,
possibly unbounded $A$, the graph-domain theorem still gives the
Schroedinger-picture derivative stated above, but no Heisenberg-picture
identification is asserted here. The spreads
$\Delta A(t_{0})$ and $\Delta K(t_{0})$ are preparation spreads in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]], and the theorem's clause (d)
records that when $f'(t_{0})=0$ the quotient supplies no timescale at all.
downstream_uses.rem-nrqm-uncertainty-error-disturbance-d:
**Preparation spread.** For an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ and a
preparation $\rho$, the spread $\Delta_{\rho}A$ of
[[def-nrqm-uncertainty-preparation-spread]] is the standard deviation of the
outcome law that the observable and probability postulate assigns to the pair
$(\rho,A)$: it is a property of the preparation and the assigned observable,
computed from the Born law alone, and it exists only under the stated moment
hypotheses. The inequalities of
[[pthm-nrqm-uncertainty-robertson-relation]] concern these spreads and nothing
else.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the smooth time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime of [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]], with $\gamma=-g$, and let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open solution region. Let a smooth reduced dust solution on $\Omega$ have a nondegenerate tentative orthonormal frame for $\gamma$ of signature $(+---)$, a metric-compatible tentative connection, reconstructed algebraic Weyl tensor $C$, prescribed curvature $\overline R$, and dust Schouten tensor $S$ as in [[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]] and [[def-gr-dust-electric-magnetic-weyl-variables-and-schouten]]. Let $\Sigma\subseteq\Omega$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface for $g$, with future unit normal $\mathfrak n$. Interpret the metric domain relative to $\Omega$: $D_\Omega^+(\Sigma)$ consists of points in $\Omega$ such that every past-inextendible causal curve in $\Omega$ through the point meets $\Sigma$, and $D_\Omega^-(\Sigma)$ is defined with future-inextendible curves ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (d), with $\Omega$ as ambient region). Allow $r\geq0$, with a smooth unit timelike $U$ prescribed also where $r=0$. Assume the parallel-comoving gauge and precisely the reduced equations
$$e_0=U,\quad\Gamma_0{}^i{}_j=0,\quad T^i{}_{0a}=0,\quad\Delta^i{}_{j0a}=0,\quad P_{ab}=Q_{ab}=0,\quad q=U(r)+r\chi=0.$$
Here $a,b=1,2,3$, the first torsion index is the output index, and $P_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are the symmetric tracefree evolution projections of [[lem-gr-dust-reduced-evolution-equations]]. No spatial torsion or spatial curvature residual is assumed zero. Define $F_{jkl}=\nabla^i(C_{ijkl}-\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j})$, $P_a=F_{0a0}$, and $Q_a=-\epsilon_a{}^{bc}F_{0bc}/2$. Then the spatial components of $(T,\Delta)$ and the vectors $(P,Q)$ satisfy the explicit closed linear homogeneous system constructed in the proof. Its principal part is transport along $U$ for $T,\Delta$ and the curl pair
$$e_0(P_a)+\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(Q_c),\qquad e_0(Q_a)-\tfrac12\epsilon_a{}^{bc}e_b(P_c).$$
It is symmetric hyperbolic on every spacelike initial hypersurface, including one tilted relative to $U$. If all residuals vanish initially, they vanish on the metric domain of determination of that surface relative to $\Omega$, namely $D_\Omega^+(\Sigma)\cup D_\Omega^-(\Sigma)$ as in [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], with causal curves taken inside the open solution region $\Omega$. Consequently the tentative connection is Levi--Civita, its actual curvature equals $\overline R$, and the resulting metric satisfies the full Einstein-dust equation. The conclusion uses neither division by $r$ nor hypersurface orthogonality of $U$.

[F2] The reconstruction gives all algebraic Weyl symmetries, $\overline R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\gamma_{i[k}S_{l]j}-\gamma_{j[k}S_{l]i}$, and the prescribed Einstein Ricci tensor. [[def-cm13-canonical-map]] defines the dimension-aware canonical maps of the
presentation by $C^{*}\omega_{2}=\omega_{1}$; a lower-dimensional map is a
symplectic immersion, while equal-dimensional maps have the matrix test
$DC^{\mathsf T}J\,DC=J$ and determinant consequence $|\det DC|=1$.
[[pthm-cm13-flow-preservation]] proves that
the Hamiltonian evolution itself is canonical on its actual time-slice
domains — the two-form, the bracket and the determinant are preserved locally
in time, also when the Hamiltonian depends on time. Its time slices have the
$C^1$ regularity stated there; the separate fixed-map field-transport
theorem applies to an individual time slice only when it has additional
$C^2$ regularity.
[[pthm-cm13-dynamics-transport-under-canonical-maps]] proves that an
equal-dimensional local canonical transformation conjugates Hamiltonian
fields and transports the model's Hamiltonian systems and brackets.
[[pthm-cm13-liouville]] uses the phase-volume form
$\Omega=\omega^{\wedge n}/n!$ to prove conservation of phase volume: on its
actual domains the Hamiltonian evolution preserves the Lebesgue measure in
every full-dimensional canonical chart, under the stated Axiom of Countable
Choice used by the change-of-variables step. The phase-volume unit is action
to the power $3N$. [[pthm-cm13-generating-functions]] closes the
constructive part: first- and second-kind generating functions with
nondegenerate mixed derivative generate canonical local diffeomorphisms of
the presentation, the local converse holds under an invertible
$(q,Q)$-projection, and a time-dependent generating function carries the
identity $p\cdot dq-H\,dt=P\cdot dQ-K\,dt+dS$ with $K=H+S_{t}$ and transports
Hamilton's equations between the two descriptions; the underlying calculus
of generating functions is that of [[cm-math-canonical]].

The concrete charges are then proved against explicit hypotheses on the
declared potential. [[pthm-cm08-time-energy]] shows that the time-translation
datum, with its parameter measured in seconds, satisfies the model identity
exactly for autonomous representatives,
proves conservation of $K+U$ in the autonomous global potential branch, and,
in that branch, exhibits the failure of conservation along an actual maximal
motion whenever $\partial_{t}U$ is nonzero at a state.
[[pthm-cm08-translation]] uses a dimensionless direction vector and a
length-valued parameter to convert the differential condition
$\sum_{i}a\cdot\nabla_{x_{i}}U=0$, equivalently invariance of $U$ along
simultaneous translation segments contained in $Q$, into conservation of the total-momentum
component $a\cdot P$ in the global potential branch, with the failure rate of
the sharpness clause. Comparing endpoints across excluded segments additionally
requires agreement of the component constants specified in that theorem.
[[pthm-cm08-rotation]] does the same for the rotation
family with dimensionless axis vector $a$ and radian-valued parameter in that
branch, whose charge is the component $a\cdot J$
of the total angular momentum about the inertial origin, together with its
full vector form for rotationally invariant potentials; and
[[pthm-cm08-boost-boundary]] treats the Galilean boost datum with dimensionless
direction $a$ and velocity-valued family parameter, whose charge has mass-length
units and is conserved under the differential translation condition in the global potential
branch. It records that an admissible boosted curve is a motion exactly when the
potential gradients at its paired endpoints agree; this follows when the
joining segments lie in $Q$ or the full endpoint-invariance criterion holds, gives the general rate $K_{a}'=t\,a\cdot F_{\mathrm{tot}}$, and
marks the boundary: Galilean frame availability is kinematic, while the boost
charge is a property of the model's Lagrangian.
[[pthm-cm08-moving-chart-energy-function]] supplies the
bookkeeping of a time-dependent coordinate description: the chart energy
function differs from the inertial mechanical energy by
$\langle X_{t},\mathsf M x'\rangle$, is conserved along chart solutions when
the substituted Lagrangian has no explicit time dependence, and the chart
description of every motion of the global potential branch solves that chart
equation. The page closes with
[[rem-cm08-external-symmetry-breaking]]: in the global potential branch, uniform fields,
confining or time-dependent potentials can break the corresponding symmetries,
residual forces destroy charges at the computed rates, "the Hamiltonian is
conserved" is not a statement about the inertial mechanical energy in a
moving chart, no converse from conservation to symmetry is asserted, and
every conservation statement is a conditional deduction of the model rather
than an empirical finding.

page_maintenance.affected_use:
Worked checks for [[cm13-symplectic-geometry-and-canonical-methods]].
[[ex-cm13-fundamental-brackets-and-evolution-checks]] evaluates the bracket
and the evolution law on one-label data of the force branch, where
$\{x^{a},H\}=m^{-1}p_{a}$ and $\{p_{a},H\}=-U_{x^{a}}$, and checks the
oscillator case of the derived bracket algebra.
[[ex-cm13-isotropic-oscillator-flow-symplectic-and-volume-checks]] carries
the isotropic oscillator through its explicit flow, verifying the matrix
and determinant tests of canonicity on each two-dimensional block and the
area and energy checks of the motion.
[[ex-cm13-free-particle-flow-generating-function]] exhibits the free-particle
flow $Q=q+(t/m)p$ as generated by the first-kind action function
$S_{t}(q,Q)=-m\lvert Q-q\rvert^{2}/(2t)$, with the projection check and the
exact change of the canonical one-form.
[[ex-cm13-point-transformation-generating-function-and-projection]]
generates the point-transformation chart transition
$(q,\pi)\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\mathsf T}\pi)$, from generalized momentum $\pi$
to Cartesian momentum, using the second-kind action function $S(q,P)=P\cdot
X(q)$. It shows that the $(q,Q)$-projection is nowhere invertible, so the
local converse's invertible-projection hypothesis cannot be dropped; the
momentum shift supplies the contrast. [[ex-cm13-determinant-tests-for-linear-canonical-maps]]
proves on explicit linear maps that $\det A=1$ is equivalent to canonicity
in dimension two but strictly weaker in dimension four, by the
volume-preserving shear with $\{Q^{2},P_{1}\}=1$.
[[ex-cm13-verlet-map-of-the-mechanical-splitting-is-canonical]] verifies that
the velocity-Verlet step of the model's mechanical splitting is a canonical
map of the presentation: the drift and kick are exact flows with unit
determinant, their composite preserves the two-form, and the oscillator
instance is computed explicitly.

page_maintenance.affected_use:
The two counterexamples exhibit the hypotheses that cannot be dropped.
[[cex-cm14-harmonic-model-critical-fibre]] shows that the zero-energy
level of the one-degree-of-freedom harmonic datum in its declared
generalized-coordinate presentation is a compact connected common level
set that is a single point, not a torus: compactness and connectedness
alone do not give the toral conclusion, regularity is indispensable.
[[cex-cm14-free-particle-noncompact-fibre]] uses the three-integral free-particle datum
$(H,p_1,p_2)$ on $p_3>0$: each common fibre at
$(E,c_1,c_2)$ with $2mE>c_1^2+c_2^2$ is a connected copy of
$\mathbb R^3$ that is
noncompact and carries no period at all, so the compactness hypothesis of
[[pthm-cm14-regular-tori]] is indispensable too. The published
mathematical obstruction
[[prop-period-lattice-monodromy-obstructs-global-action-angle-coordinates]]
and the refuted global statement
[[fs-liouville-arnold-gives-global-action-angle-coordinates-on-the-entire-manifold]]
record the complementary global failure: local action-angle coordinates
need not patch to a single-valued global chart even when all fibres are
regular and compact, so no universal torus chart is claimed. Finally,
[[ex-cm14-oscillator-caustic-check]] exhibits the local caustic of the
oscillator family: the mixed derivative $S_{x\alpha}$ of the complete
integral is unbounded at the conjugate times $\omega t\in\pi\mathbb Z$,
and the family of model solutions through a fixed event refocuses there,
which is why the Hamilton–Jacobi statements of this page are local in
time and carry no claim across a caustic.

page_maintenance.affected_use:
[[ex-cm16-pendulum-equilibrium-checks]] works the ideal pendulum in the angle
chart with $m=1\ \mathrm{kg}$, $\ell=1\ \mathrm m$ and
$g=9.81\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$: the downward equilibrium is a strict minimum,
hence Lyapunov stable and not attracting, with the purely imaginary
linearisation frequencies $\pm i\,3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$; the upward
equilibrium has the negative Hessian $-mg\ell$ and is unstable, with the real
rates $\pm3\sqrt{109}/10\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
[[ex-cm16-linearization-and-growth-checks]] computes the flows and growth
rates of two dimensionless one-label Cartesian models in $\mathbb R^3$: the
harmonic force $F(\mathbf q)=-\mathbf q$ has an orthogonal rotation flow, so
every finite-time growth rate vanishes and every existing Lyapunov exponent is
$0$; the repulsive force $F(\mathbf q)=\mathbf q$ has exact rates $\pm1$ along
its eigendirections and positive Lyapunov exponent $1$ at equilibrium.
[[ex-cm16-isotropic-oscillator-return-map-check]] shows the
three-dimensional isotropic force model's stroboscopic map at half period to
be minus the identity on its six-dimensional phase space: every state is
periodic, the periodic points are dense, but the map is neither topologically
mixing nor sensitive, so continuous maps with dense periodic points need not
be chaotic in the page's stated sense.
[[ex-cm16-pulse-horseshoe-data-check]] evaluates the constants of the pulsed
horseshoe on its invariant axis at $a=100$: the coding box $R=13$, the
radicands in $[74,126]$, the contraction factor $1/\sqrt{74}$, the fixed
points $1\pm\sqrt{101}$, the limiting kick composition, and the axial physical
bounds $13\ \mathrm m$ and
$26\pi\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ at $\ell_0=1\ \mathrm m$, $m=1\ \mathrm{kg}$,
$\omega_0=2\pi\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.

stress, the displacement equation at $c_L=\sqrt{(\lambda+2\mu_s)/\rho_0}$ and
the positive strain-energy density. [[ex-cm17-string-modes-and-tail-check]]
solves a two-mode fixed-end string exactly, cross-checks the d'Alembert
formula, and evaluates the $O(N^{-4})$ tail bound at $N=1$.
[[ex-cm17-spring-chain-limit-numbers]] compares the cyclic mass-spring chain
with the travelling standing wave: the exact discrete frequency and nodal
error, the evaluated $O(a^{3/2})$ bound at $N=100$, and the second-order
dispersion error in the spacing. [[ex-cm17-riemann-shock-and-rarefaction-check]] verifies an
explicit Rankine-Hugoniot shock with its entropy coefficients under the countable-choice Lebesgue weak formulation and a
rarefaction fan with its initial trace in the scalar weak formulation.
[[ex-cm17-channel-flow-and-no-slip-check]] solves the steady viscous channel
exactly (Poiseuille flux and centre speed, Couette vorticity, uniqueness in
the ansatz) under the adopted no-slip wall data.
[[ex-cm17-periodic-shear-exact-solution-check]] exhibits the sinusoidal shear
as an exact steady Euler solution in the scaled variables of the periodic cell, shows it fails the
viscous projected equation, and classifies the steady periodic viscous shears
as constants. [[cex-cm17-traction-symmetry-without-stress-matrix]] refutes
the claim that the reversed-normal convention alone forces a stress matrix:
the continuous balanced-looking field $t(n)=|n_1|n$ has no representing
matrix, so the balance hypothesis of the Cauchy-tetrahedron theorem is
essential.

page_maintenance.affected_use:
The chaos material is built on the two local mathematical supplier pages
[[cm-math-chaos]] and [[cm-math-kam]].
[[def-cm16-chaos-list-for-model-maps]] fixes one precise chaos list for the
stroboscopic, Poincare-return and autonomous time-one maps on invariant
domains: continuity, topological mixing, dense periodic points and
sensitive dependence. This item makes no pairwise-independence claim and
records that fixed linear coordinate rescalings preserve the list; numerical
portraits do not establish its clauses. [[pthm-cm16-separatrix-splitting-and-horseshoe]]
then adopts a smooth $P$-periodic one-label force model on full Cartesian
configuration space $\mathbb R^3$: the pulse acts on an invariant axis, and
the two transverse directions have explicitly adopted inverted-oscillator
forces. For every pulse width below a threshold depending only on the
dimensionless amplitude $a\ge100$ and the bump, the full physical stroboscopic
map has a compact invariant set on the axis conjugate to the two-sign shift
and chaotic in the stated sense; its fixed points are hyperbolic in the full
six-dimensional phase space and its homoclinic points are transverse there.
The coded states satisfy the bounds $\lvert Q\rvert\le R\ell_0$ and
$\lvert\Pi\rvert\le m\ell_0\omega_0R$ with $R=\sqrt a+3$. The countable and
dependent choice assumptions are inherited from the supplier and declared.
[[pthm-cm16-two-rotor-kam]] treats the complementary nearly integrable
two-rotor model with the adopted potential $E_0\varepsilon\cos\theta_1
\cos\theta_2$: for every Diophantine exponent $\tau>1$ and a constant $c>0$
determined by the declared dimensionless data, every $0<\alpha<c$ and
$0<\varepsilon\le c\alpha^2$ give a positive-measure set of Diophantine
frequencies whose tori persist as $C^1$ Lagrangian embeddings carrying
quasi-periodic motion with physical angular frequencies $\omega_0\nu_i$
($\omega_0=\sqrt{E_0/\mathcal I}$); the complement of that set, resonant gaps,
chaotic diffusion and all empirical realizations are explicitly out of scope.
Finally [[pthm-cm16-recurrence-for-finite-volume-models]], under the
countable choice assumption inherited from the phase-volume theorem, proves
Poincare recurrence at unit time steps for a bounded invariant Borel set with
compact closure in an autonomous potential phase domain and a flow complete on
that set. Its proof extends local phase-volume preservation by a finite cover
and time subdivision; the conclusion is almost-everywhere, with no return-time
or individual-state claim.

Contact forces are defined by [[def-cm17-traction-and-stress]] and adopted by
[[post-cm17-contact-force-model]] (continuous body forces and Cauchy
tractions), and the balance principles are adopted in force form by
[[post-cm17-momentum-balance]]. From them
[[pthm-cm17-stress-matrix-and-symmetry]] derives the existence, uniqueness,
reversed-normal identity and symmetry of the stress matrix by Cauchy's
tetrahedron and the couple-free torque balance, and
[[pthm-cm17-momentum-equation]] localizes the balances into the model's
momentum equation $\rho D_tu=\rho b+\operatorname{div}\sigma$. Two
constitutive branches are then carried through complete deductions: the
small-strain isotropic linear elastic branch
([[post-cm17-linear-elastic-constitutive]],
[[pthm-cm17-linear-elastic-equation-of-motion]],
[[pthm-cm17-elastic-plane-wave-speeds]]) with the displacement equation
$\rho_0\partial_t^2\xi=\rho_0b+\mu_s\Delta\xi+(\lambda+\mu_s)\nabla\operatorname{div}\xi$
and its longitudinal and transverse speeds, and the fluid branch
([[post-cm17-fluid-constitutive]]) with the chain limit
[[pthm-cm17-chain-limit-of-the-string-model]] and the string solutions
[[pthm-cm17-string-wave-solutions]] on the one-dimensional side and the local
periodic evolution theorem
[[pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-evolution]] on the
three-dimensional side, using separately adopted incompressible inviscid or Newtonian stress, explicit length/velocity/time scales and conversion of its unit-torus lifespan to physical time. [[rem-cm17-boundary-regularity-and-scope]] closes the
page by recording the ideal boundary data, the regularity limits that exclude
shocks and interfaces from the classical identities, the constitutive
validity regimes, the deliberately open specialist scopes and the
model-versus-nature status of every result.
